# Actor Spring Boot Starter

> A Spring Boot starter that runs Pekko typed actors as Spring beans. Add `@EnableActorSupport`, implement `SpringActor` (or `SpringShardedActor` for cluster sharding), and use `SpringActorSystem` to spawn, look up and message actors. The public API has no Pekko types: use the starter's types, not raw Pekko or Akka APIs. It ships as `io.github.seonwkim:actor-spring-boot-starter` (add `actor-spring-boot-starter-cluster` for cluster mode), needs Java 21+ and Spring Boot 3.5+, and is configured with typed `spring.actor.*` properties.

The full text of the Getting Started page and every guide, with code inlined, is in [llms-full.txt](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/llms-full.txt): read it when the links below are not enough.

## Getting started

- [Introduction](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/): what the starter is for, the modules, and how actors fit into a Spring Boot application
- [Getting Started](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/getting-started/): dependency, `@EnableActorSupport`, a first actor and an HTTP endpoint that asks it, in Java and Kotlin
- [Migrating from 0.x](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/migrating-from-0x/): new coordinates, packages and APIs in 1.0, step by step

## Guides

### Core

- [Actors](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/core/actors/): define actors as beans, actor ids, spawn/get/getOrSpawn/exists/stop, custom contexts, child actors
- [Messaging](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/core/messaging/): tell, ask with timeouts and `onTimeout`, replying, asking from inside an actor, message adapters
- [Supervision](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/core/supervision/): stop/restart/resume strategies (default stop), limits, what a restart keeps, supervising children
- [Behaviors, Timers and Watching](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/core/behaviors/): the behavior builder, `withState`, signals, timers, watch, `pipeToSelf`, no stash
- [Routers](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/core/routers/): spread messages across a pool of worker actors; routing strategies
- [Pub/Sub Topics](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/core/pub-sub-topics/): one-to-many messaging where publishers do not know the subscribers
- [Receptionist](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/core/receptionist/): find actors by service key, once or by subscribing to changes
- [Dispatchers and Mailboxes](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/core/dispatchers/): choose the threads an actor runs on: blocking, Spring executors, virtual threads; mailboxes
- [Logging](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/core/logging/): MDC values, request ids and actor tags in log lines

### Cluster

- [Sharded Actors](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/cluster/sharded-actors/): one actor per entity id, spread across a cluster; roles, passivation, shard leases
- [Singletons](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/cluster/singletons/): one actor in the whole cluster with `asClusterSingleton()`, where it runs, handover and leases
- [Cluster Formation](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/cluster/cluster-formation/): join through seed nodes, Kubernetes, a JDBC table, Redis or your own store
- [Split Brain and Leases](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/cluster/split-brain-and-leases/): which side of a network split stays up; leases in a JDBC table, Redis or your own store
- [Replicated Data](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/cluster/replicated-data/): maps, counters and sets copied to every node, with local, majority or all consistency

### Data

- [State in a Database](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/data/state-in-a-database/): load on start and save on change with Spring Data, JDBC or R2DBC, without event sourcing
- [Event-Sourced Actors](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/data/event-sourcing/): store events instead of state with actor-persistence, recovery, snapshots
- [Projections](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/data/projections/): read persisted events into Spring Data or Kafka, exactly once or at least once

### Streaming

- [Reactor Streams](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/streaming/reactor-streams/): a `Mono` of an ask, a `Flux` into an actor with backpressure, a `Flux` out of an actor (`actor-streams`)
- [Streaming to Clients](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/streaming/streaming-to-clients/): Server-Sent Events, WebSocket (`ActorWebSocketHandler`) and gRPC (`ActorGrpc`) from actors

### Operations

- [Running in Production](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/operations/production/): graceful shutdown, health checks, Kubernetes probes, a production checklist, GraalVM native images
- [Monitoring](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/operations/monitoring/): actor, mailbox, dispatcher, cluster and sharding meters, the actors endpoint, tracing, Grafana dashboard and alerts
- [Deployments](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/operations/deployments/): rolling, canary and blue-green deployments, and message compatibility across versions
- [Configuration Reference](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/operations/configuration/): every `spring.actor.*` key with its default

### More guides

- [Testing](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/testing/): the `@ActorTest` slice, multi-node clusters in one JVM, contract suites for your own `PeerRegistry` or `LeaseStore`
- [Kotlin](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/kotlin/): the `actor-kotlin` module: suspend ask and spawn, reified helpers
- [AI Agents](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/ai-agents/): one sharded actor per agent, supervised conversations, non-blocking model calls, approvals

## Examples

- [Examples overview](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/): every runnable example app, what it shows, and a learning path
- [Simple](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/simple/): basic actors, ask and restart in a single application
- [Cluster](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/cluster/): sharded actors and a singleton across three nodes
- [Synchronization](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/synchronization/): an actor counter compared with database and Redis locks
- [Chat](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/chat/): real-time chat with WebSocket, sharded rooms and pub/sub topics
- [AI Agent](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/agent/): an AI agent as an actor: tools, approvals, snapshots
- [Persistence](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/persistence/): actor state with JPA: current state, event log and snapshots
- [Metrics](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/metrics/): actor metrics through Micrometer and Prometheus
- [Logging](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/logging/): MDC, tags and request ids in actor logs
- [Virtual Threads](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/virtual-threads/): actors on a virtual-thread dispatcher
- [Kotlin](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/kotlin/): the starter from Kotlin with coroutines
- [Kubernetes](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/kubernetes/): a cluster on Kubernetes: discovery, rollouts and monitoring

## Reference

- [How to Contribute](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/contributing/): report bugs and propose changes through GitHub Issues
- [Spring Conventions](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/contributing/spring-conventions/): how the starter compares with the conventions of other Spring projects
